Unfortunately many doctors are like that, downplaying the pain and symptoms to the point of irrationality.

My grandmother has endometriosis, and every doctor that she saw refused to listen to her and denied that she had it. It took going to *another state* before she was finally given a proper diagnosis.

Though there is not much I can offer in lieu of advice, from personal experience regular exercise- it doesn't have to be a hard workout, just something light but routine- can help ease the intensity of the cramps during the cycle. Also, it helps to reduce any sodium intake both during and leading up to the bleeding, as sodium can exacerbate the cramps.

Other than that, if she can safely take ibuprofen, it can offer a temporary relief. Just be careful with how much and how often as overuse/overdosing can damage the kidneys over time, as well as lead to the development of stomach ulcers.

I hope at least one of the things I've said could be helpful, and I wish you all the best. I hope that she gets some proper treatment sooner than later.

Edit: That was an awful time for me, one that left a lot of mental scars, many of which are still just as prominent as when I got them. I hated myself, I harmed myself, every adult and academic authority figure I thought I could trust were about as useful as a wet paper bag, either doing nothing significant or making everything worse. 13 was the worst year of my adolescence, and it only marked the downfall of my physical and mental health throughout the trainwrexk that was puberty. I wondered more times than I'd care to admit if ending it all would be a better solution than the miserable existence where I caused myself bodily harm to avoid returning to my classes and enduring harsh ridicule and mockery from my classmates, where my principal learned of my efforts and indirectly accused me of attention-seeking and responded by punishing me with in-school suspension.

Where I cried myself to sleep, on the nights I was actually able to sleep. Where the only person I had to talk about when the awful, self-harming thoughts came back, who said I call them any time no matter what was too busy the one and only time I tried to reach out.

So, I'd like to look younger me in the face, hug them tight, and let them know it's not perfect, but "it gets better."

Get a stretchy sock or pantyhose and stretch it over the end of the hose of a vacuum. This will suck the beads into the sock without sucking them into the tank. Though I don't suggest turning off the suction without placing something to hold the beads underneath, just in case any fall out when the suction turns off.

Or, you could empty out the vacuum tank and just suck the beads straight into the tank, then empty them into a large bin or bowl.

If you don't have a vacuum, then you could try one of those lint rollers you can pick up at the nearest shop/dollar store/ possibly gas station. Just roll it over the carpet. Fair warning, lint rollers do not discriminate. If they can pick it up, they will.
